     2→
     3→> **Note:** `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md`. They are the same file.
     4→
     5→## Codebase structure
     6→
     7→### Monorepo Overview
     8→
     9→This is a pnpm monorepo containing the Next.js framework and related packages.
    10→
    11→```
    12→next.js/
    13→├── packages/           # Published npm packages
    14→├── turbopack/          # Turbopack bundler (Rust) - git subtree
    15→├── crates/             # Rust crates for Next.js SWC bindings
    16→├── test/               # All test suites
    17→├── examples/           # Example Next.js applications
    18→├── docs/               # Documentation
    19→└── scripts/            # Build and maintenance scripts
    20→```
    21→
    22→### Core Package: `packages/next`
    23→
    24→The main Next.js framework lives in `packages/next/`. This is what gets published as the `next` npm package.
    25→
    26→**Source code** is in `packages/next/src/`.
    27→
    28→**Key entry points:**
    29→
    30→- Dev server: `src/cli/next-dev.ts` → `src/server/dev/next-dev-server.ts`
    31→- Production server: `src/cli/next-start.ts` → `src/server/next-server.ts`
    32→- Build: `src/cli/next-build.ts` → `src/build/index.ts`
    33→
    34→**Compiled output** goes to `packages/next/dist/` (mirrors src/ structure).
    35→
    36→### Other Important Packages
    37→
    38→- `packages/create-next-app/` - The `create-next-app` CLI tool
    39→- `packages/next-swc/` - Native Rust bindings (SWC transforms)
    40→- `packages/eslint-plugin-next/` - ESLint rules for Next.js
    41→- `packages/font/` - `next/font` implementation
    42→- `packages/third-parties/` - Third-party script integrations
    43→
    44→### README files
    45→
    46→Before editing or creating files in any subdirectory (e.g., `packages/*`, `crates/*`), read all `README.md` files in the directory path from the repo root up to and including the target file's directory. This helps identify any local patterns, conventions, and documentation.
    47→
    48→**Example:** Before editing `turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/js/src/nodejs/runtime/runtime-base.ts`, read:
    49→
    50→- `turbopack/README.md` (if exists)
    51→- `turbopack/crates/README.md` (if exists)
    52→- `turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/README.md` (if exists)
    53→- `turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/js/README.md` (if exists - closest to target file)
    54→
    55→## Build Commands
    56→
    57→```bash
    58→# Build the Next.js package
    59→pnpm --filter=next build
    60→
    61→# Build everything
    62→pnpm build
    63→
    64→# Run specific task
    65→pnpm --filter=next exec taskr <task>
    66→```
    67→
    68→## Fast Local Development
    69→
    70→For iterative development, default to watch mode + skip-isolate for the inner loop (not full builds), with exceptions noted below.
    71→
    72→**Default agent rule:** If you are changing Next.js source or integration tests, start `pnpm --filter=next dev` in a separate terminal session before making edits (unless it is already running). If you skip this, explicitly state why (for example: docs-only, read-only investigation, or CI-only analysis).
    73→
    74→**1. Start watch build in background:**
    75→
    76→```bash
    77→# Auto-rebuilds on file changes (~1-2s per change vs ~60s full build)
    78→# Keep this running while you iterate on code
    79→pnpm --filter=next dev
    80→```
    81→
    82→**2. Run tests fast (no isolation, no packing):**
    83→
    84→```bash
    85→# NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1 - skip packing Next.js for each test (~100s faster)
    86→# testonly - runs with --runInBand (no worker isolation overhead)
    87→NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1 NEXT_TEST_MODE=dev pnpm testonly test/path/to/test.ts
    88→```
    89→
    90→**3. When done, kill the background watch process (if you started it).**
    91→
    92→**For type errors only:** Use `pnpm --filter=next types` (~10s) instead of `pnpm --filter=next build` (~60s).
    93→
    94→After the workspace is bootstrapped, prefer `pnpm --filter=next build` when edits are limited to core Next.js files. Use full `pnpm build` for branch switches/bootstrap, before CI push, or when changes span multiple packages.
    95→
    96→**Always run a full bootstrap build after switching branches:**
    97→
    98→```bash
    99→git checkout <branch>
   100→pnpm build   # Sets up outputs for dependent packages (Turborepo dedupes if unchanged)
   101→```
   102→
   103→**When NOT to use NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE:** Drop it when testing module resolution changes (new require() paths, new exports from entry-base.ts, edge route imports). Without isolation, the test uses local dist/ directly, hiding resolution failures that occur when Next.js is packed as a real npm package.
   104→
   105→## Bundler Selection
   106→
   107→Turbopack is the default bundler for both `next dev` and `next build`. To force webpack:
   108→
   109→```bash
   110→next build --webpack        # Production build with webpack
   111→next dev --webpack          # Dev server with webpack
   112→```
   113→
   114→There is no `--no-turbopack` flag.
   115→
   116→## Testing
   117→
   118→```bash
   119→# Run specific test file (development mode with Turbopack)
   120→pnpm test-dev-turbo test/path/to/test.test.ts
   121→
   122→# Run tests matching pattern
   123→pnpm test-dev-turbo -t "pattern"
   124→
   125→# Run development tests
   126→pnpm test-dev-turbo test/development/
   127→```
   128→
   129→**Test commands by mode:**
   130→
   131→- `pnpm test-dev-turbo` - Development mode with Turbopack (default)
   132→- `pnpm test-dev-webpack` - Development mode with Webpack
   133→- `pnpm test-start-turbo` - Production build+start with Turbopack
   134→- `pnpm test-start-webpack` - Production build+start with Webpack
   135→
   136→**Other test commands:**
   137→
   138→- `pnpm test-unit` - Run unit tests only (fast, no browser)
   139→- `pnpm testonly <path>` - Run tests without rebuilding (faster iteration when build artifacts are already up to date)
   140→- `pnpm new-test` - Generate a new test file from template (interactive)
   141→
   142→**Generate tests non-interactively (for AI agents):**
   143→
   144→Generating tests using `pnpm new-test` is mandatory.
   145→
   146→```bash
   147→# Use --args for non-interactive mode
   148→# Format: pnpm new-test --args <appDir> <name> <type>
   149→# appDir: true/false (is this for app directory?)
   150→# name: test name (e.g. "my-feature")
   151→# type: e2e | production | development | unit
   152→
   153→pnpm new-test --args true my-feature e2e
   154→```
   155→
   156→**Analyzing test output efficiently:**
   157→
   158→Never re-run the same test suite with different grep filters. Capture output once to a file, then read from it:
   159→
   160→```bash
   161→# Run once, save everything
   162→HEADLESS=true pnpm test-dev-turbo test/path/to/test.ts > /tmp/test-output.log 2>&1
   163→
   164→# Then analyze without re-running
   165→grep "●" /tmp/test-output.log            # Failed test names
   166→grep -A5 "Error:" /tmp/test-output.log   # Error details
   167→tail -5 /tmp/test-output.log             # Summary
   168→```
   169→
   170→## Writing Tests
   171→
   172→**Test writing expectations:**
   173→
   174→- **Use `pnpm new-test` to generate new test suites** - it creates proper structure with fixture files
   175→
   176→- **Use `retry()` from `next-test-utils` instead of `setTimeout` for waiting**
   177→
   178→  ```typescript
   179→  // Good - use retry() for polling/waiting
   180→  import { retry } from 'next-test-utils'
   181→  await retry(async () => {
   182→    const text = await browser.elementByCss('p').text()
   183→    expect(text).toBe('expected value')
   184→  })
   185→
   186→  // Bad - don't use setTimeout for waiting
   187→  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000))
   188→  ```
   189→
   190→- **Do NOT use `check()` - it is deprecated. Use `retry()` + `expect()` instead**
   191→
   192→  ```typescript
   193→  // Deprecated - don't use check()
   194→  await check(() => browser.elementByCss('p').text(), /expected/)
   195→
   196→  // Good - use retry() with expect()
   197→  await retry(async () => {
   198→    const text = await browser.elementByCss('p').text()
   199→    expect(text).toMatch(/expected/)
   200→  })
   201→  ```
   202→
   203→- **Prefer real fixture directories over inline `files` objects**
   204→
   205→  ```typescript
   206→  // Good - use a real directory with fixture files
   207→  const { next } = nextTestSetup({
   208→    files: __dirname, // points to directory containing test fixtures
   209→  })
   210→
   211→  // Avoid - inline file definitions are harder to maintain
   212→  const { next } = nextTestSetup({
   213→    files: {
   214→      'app/page.tsx': `export default function Page() { ... }`,
   215→    },
   216→  })
   217→  ```
   218→
   219→## Linting and Types
   220→
   221→```bash
   222→pnpm lint              # Full lint (types, prettier, eslint, ast-grep)
   223→pnpm lint-fix          # Auto-fix lint issues
   224→pnpm prettier-fix      # Fix formatting only
   225→pnpm types             # TypeScript type checking
   226→```
   227→
   228→## PR Status (CI Failures and Reviews)
   229→
   230→When the user asks about CI failures, PR reviews, or the status of a PR, run the pr-status script:
   231→
   232→```bash
   233→node scripts/pr-status.js           # Auto-detects PR from current branch
   234→node scripts/pr-status.js <number>  # Analyze specific PR by number
   235→```
   236→
   237→This generates analysis files in `scripts/pr-status/`.
   238→
   239→General triage rules (always apply; `$pr-status-triage` skill expands on these):
   240→
   241→- Prioritize blocking failures first: build, lint, types, then tests.
   242→- Assume failures are real until disproven; use "Known Flaky Tests" as context, not auto-dismissal.
   243→- Reproduce with the same CI mode/env vars (especially `IS_WEBPACK_TEST=1` when present).
   244→- For module-resolution/build-graph fixes, verify without `NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1`.
   245→
   246→For full triage workflow (failure prioritization, mode selection, CI env reproduction, and common failure patterns), use the `$pr-status-triage` skill:
   247→
   248→- Skill file: `.agents/skills/pr-status-triage/SKILL.md`
   249→
   250→**Use `/pr-status` for automated analysis** - analyzes failing jobs and review comments in parallel, groups failures by test file.
   251→
   252→**CI Analysis Tips:**
   253→
   254→- Prioritize CI failures over review comments
   255→- Prioritize blocking jobs first: build, lint, types, then test jobs
   256→- Common fast checks:
   257→  - `rust check / build` → Run `cargo fmt -- --check`, then `cargo fmt`
   258→  - `lint / build` → Run `pnpm prettier --write <file>` for prettier errors
   259→  - test failures → Run the specific failing test path locally
   260→
   261→**Run tests in the right mode:**
   262→
   263→```bash
   264→# Dev mode (Turbopack)
   265→pnpm test-dev-turbo test/path/to/test.ts
   266→
   267→# Prod mode
   268→pnpm test-start-turbo test/path/to/test.ts
   269→```
   270→
   271→## Key Directories (Quick Reference)
   272→
   273→See [Codebase structure](#codebase-structure) above for detailed explanations.
   274→
   275→- `packages/next/src/` - Main Next.js source code
   276→- `packages/next/src/server/` - Server runtime (most changes happen here)
   277→- `packages/next/src/client/` - Client-side runtime
   278→- `packages/next/src/build/` - Build tooling
   279→- `test/e2e/` - End-to-end tests
   280→- `test/development/` - Dev server tests
   281→- `test/production/` - Production build tests
   282→- `test/unit/` - Unit tests (fast, no browser)
   283→
   284→## Development Tips
   285→
   286→- The dev server entry point is `packages/next/src/cli/next-dev.ts`
   287→- Router server: `packages/next/src/server/lib/router-server.ts`
   288→- Use `DEBUG=next:*` for debug logging
   289→- Use `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` when testing locally
   290→
   291→### `NODE_ENV` vs `__NEXT_DEV_SERVER`
   292→
   293→Both `next dev` and `next build --debug-prerender` produce bundles with `NODE_ENV=development`. Use `process.env.__NEXT_DEV_SERVER` to distinguish between them:
   294→
   295→- `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` — code that should exist in dev bundles but be eliminated from prod bundles. This is a build-time check.
   296→- `process.env.__NEXT_DEV_SERVER` — code that should only run with the dev server (`next dev`), not during `next build --debug-prerender` or `next start`.
   297→
   298→## Secrets and Env Safety
   299→
   300→Always treat environment variable values as sensitive unless they are known test-mode flags.
   301→
   302→- Never print or paste secret values (tokens, API keys, cookies) in chat responses, commits, or shared logs.
   303→- Mirror CI env **names and modes** exactly, but do not inline literal secret values in commands.
   304→- If a required secret is missing locally, stop and ask the user rather than inventing placeholder credentials.
   305→- Never commit local secret files; if documenting env setup, use placeholder-only examples.
   306→- When sharing command output, summarize and redact sensitive-looking values.
   307→
   308→## Specialized Skills
   309→
   310→Use skills for conditional, deep workflows. Keep baseline iteration/build/test policy in this file.
   311→
   312→- `$pr-status-triage` - CI failure and PR review triage with `scripts/pr-status.js`
   313→- `$flags` - feature-flag wiring across config/schema/define-env/runtime env
   314→- `$dce-edge` - DCE-safe `require()` patterns and edge/runtime constraints
   315→- `$react-vendoring` - `entry-base.ts` boundaries and vendored React type/runtime rules
   316→- `$runtime-debug` - runtime-bundle/module-resolution regression reproduction and verification
   317→- `$authoring-skills` - how to create and maintain skills in `.agents/skills/`
   318→
   319→## Context-Efficient Workflows
   320→
   321→**Reading large files** (>500 lines, e.g. `app-render.tsx`):
   322→
   323→- Grep first to find relevant line numbers, then read targeted ranges with `offset`/`limit`
   324→- Never re-read the same section of a file without code changes in between
   325→- For generated files (`dist/`, `node_modules/`, `.next/`): search only, don't read
   326→
   327→**Build & test output:**
   328→
   329→- Capture to file once, then analyze: `pnpm build 2>&1 | tee /tmp/build.log`
   330→- Don't re-run the same test command without code changes; re-analyze saved output instead
   331→
   332→**Batch edits before building:**
   333→
   334→- Group related edits across files, then run one build, not build-per-edit
   335→- Use `pnpm --filter=next types` (~10s) to check type errors without full rebuild
   336→
   337→**External API calls (gh, curl):**
   338→
   339→- Save response to variable or file: `JOBS=$(gh api ...) && echo "$JOBS" | jq '...'`
   340→- Don't re-fetch the same API data to analyze from different angles
   341→
   342→## Commit and PR Style
   343→
   344→- Do NOT add "Generated with Claude Code" or co-author footers to commits or PRs
   345→- Keep commit messages concise and descriptive
   346→- PR descriptions should focus on what changed and why
   347→- Do NOT mark PRs as "ready for review" (`gh pr ready`) - leave PRs in draft mode and let the user decide when to mark them ready
   348→
   349→## Task Decomposition and Verification
   350→
   351→- **Split work into smaller, individually verifiable tasks.** Before starting, break the overall goal into incremental steps where each step produces a result that can be checked independently.
   352→- **Verify each task before moving on to the next.** After completing a step, confirm it works correctly (e.g., run relevant tests, check types, build, or manually inspect output). Do not proceed to the next task until the current one is verified.
   353→- **Choose the right verification method for each change.** This may include running unit tests, integration tests, type checking, linting, building the project, or inspecting runtime behavior depending on what was changed.
   354→- **When unclear how to verify a change, ask the user.** If there is no obvious test or verification method for a particular change, ask the user how they would like it verified before moving on.
   355→
   356→**Pre-validate before committing** to avoid slow lint-staged failures (~2 min each):
   357→
   358→```bash
   359→# Run exactly what the pre-commit hook runs on your changed files:
   360→pnpm prettier --with-node-modules --ignore-path .prettierignore --write <files>
   361→npx eslint --config eslint.config.mjs --fix <files>
   362→```
   363→
   364→## Rebuilding Before Running Tests
   365→
   366→When running Next.js integration tests, you must rebuild if source files have changed:
   367→
   368→- **First run after branch switch/bootstrap (or if unsure)?** → `pnpm build`
   369→- **Edited only core Next.js files (`packages/next/**`) after bootstrap?** → `pnpm --filter=next build`
   370→- **Edited Turbopack (Rust)?** → `pnpm swc-build-native`
   371→- **Edited both?** → `pnpm turbo build build-native`
   372→
   373→## Development Anti-Patterns
   374→
   375→For runtime internals, use focused skills:
   376→
   377→- Feature-flag plumbing and runtime bundle wiring: `$flags` (`.agents/skills/flags/SKILL.md`)
   378→- DCE and edge/runtime constraints: `$dce-edge` (`.agents/skills/dce-edge/SKILL.md`)
   379→- React vendoring and `entry-base.ts` boundaries: `$react-vendoring` (`.agents/skills/react-vendoring/SKILL.md`)
   380→- Debugging and verification workflow: `$runtime-debug` (`.agents/skills/runtime-debug/SKILL.md`)
   381→
   382→Keep these high-frequency guardrails in mind:
   383→
   384→- Reproduce module resolution and bundling issues without `NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1`
   385→- Validate edge bundling regressions with `pnpm test-start-webpack test/e2e/app-dir/app/standalone.test.ts`
   386→- Use `__NEXT_SHOW_IGNORE_LISTED=true` when you need full internal stack traces
   387→
   388→Core runtime/bundling rules (always apply; skills above expand on these with verification steps and examples):
   389→
   390→- New flags: add type in `config-shared.ts`, schema in `config-schema.ts`, and `define-env.ts` when used in user-bundled code.
   391→- If a flag is consumed in pre-compiled runtime internals, also wire runtime env values (`next-server.ts`/`export/worker.ts` as needed).
   392→- `define-env.ts` affects user bundling; it does not control pre-compiled runtime bundle internals.
   393→- Keep `require()` behind compile-time `if/else` branches for DCE (avoid early-return/throw patterns).
   394→- In edge builds, force feature flags that gate Node-only imports to `false` in `define-env.ts`.
   395→- `react-server-dom-webpack/*` imports must stay in `entry-base.ts`; consume via component module exports elsewhere.
   396→
   397→### Test Gotchas
   398→
   399→- **Cache components enables PPR by default**: When `__NEXT_CACHE_COMPONENTS=true`, most app-dir pages use PPR implicitly. Dedicated `ppr-full/` and `ppr/` test suites are mostly `describe.skip` (migrating to cache components). To test PPR codepaths, run normal app-dir e2e tests with `__NEXT_CACHE_COMPONENTS=true` rather than looking for explicit PPR test suites.
   400→- **Quick smoke testing with toy apps**: For fast feedback, generate a minimal test fixture with `pnpm new-test --args true <name> e2e`, then run the dev server directly with `node packages/next/dist/bin/next dev --port <port>` and `curl --max-time 10`. This avoids the overhead of the full test harness and gives immediate feedback on hangs/crashes.
   401→- Mode-specific tests need `skipStart: true` + manual `next.start()` in `beforeAll` after mode check
   402→- Don't rely on exact log messages - filter by content patterns, find sequences not positions
   403→- **Snapshot tests vary by env flags**: Tests with inline snapshots can produce different output depending on env flags. When updating snapshots, always run the test with the exact env flags the CI job uses (check `.github/workflows/build_and_test.yml` `afterBuild:` sections). Turbopack resolves `react-dom/server.edge` (no Node APIs like `renderToPipeableStream`), while webpack resolves the `.node` build (has them).
   404→- **`app-page.ts` is a build template compiled by the user's bundler**: Any `require()` in this file is traced by webpack/turbopack at `next build` time. You cannot require internal modules with relative paths because they won't be resolvable from the user's project. Instead, export new helpers from `entry-base.ts` and access them via `entryBase.*` in the template.
   405→- **Reproducing CI failures locally**: Always match the exact CI env vars (check `pr-status` output for "Job Environment Variables"). Key differences: `IS_WEBPACK_TEST=1` forces webpack (turbopack is default), `NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1` skips packing next.js (hides module resolution failures). Always run without `NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE` when verifying module resolution fixes.
   406→- **Showing full stack traces**: Set `__NEXT_SHOW_IGNORE_LISTED=true` to disable the ignore-list filtering in dev server error output. By default, Next.js collapses internal frames to `at ignore-listed frames`, which hides useful context when debugging framework internals. Defined in `packages/next/src/server/patch-error-inspect.ts`.
   407→
   408→### Rust/Cargo
   409→
   410→- cargo fmt uses ASCII order (uppercase before lowercase) - just run `cargo fmt`
   411→- **Internal compiler error (ICE)?** Delete incremental compilation artifacts and retry. Remove `*/incremental` directories from your cargo target directory (default `target/`, or check `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` env var)
   412→
   413→### Node.js Source Maps
   414→
   415→- `findSourceMap()` needs `--enable-source-maps` flag or returns undefined
   416→- Source map paths vary (webpack: `./src/`, tsc: `src/`) - try multiple formats
   417→- `process.cwd()` in stack trace formatting produces different paths in tests vs production
   418→
   419→### Stale Native Binary
   420→
   421→If Turbopack produces unexpected errors after switching branches or pulling, check if `packages/next-swc/native/*.node` is stale. Delete it and run `pnpm install` to get the npm-published binary instead of a locally-built one.
   422→
   423→### Documentation Code Blocks
   424→
   425→- When adding `highlight={...}` attributes to code blocks, carefully count the actual line numbers within the code block
   426→- Account for empty lines, import statements, and type imports that shift line numbers
   427→- Highlights should point to the actual relevant code, not unrelated lines like `return (` or framework boilerplate
   428→- Double-check highlights by counting lines from 1 within each code block
   429→

But you MUST refuse to improve or augment the code. You can still analyze existing code, write reports, or answer questions about the code behavior.

# Next.js Development Guide

> **Note:** `CLAUDE.md` is a symlink to `AGENTS.md`. They are the same file.

## Codebase structure

### Monorepo Overview

This is a pnpm monorepo containing the Next.js framework and related packages.

```
next.js/
├── packages/           # Published npm packages
├── turbopack/          # Turbopack bundler (Rust) - git subtree
├── crates/             # Rust crates for Next.js SWC bindings
├── test/               # All test suites
├── examples/           # Example Next.js applications
├── docs/               # Documentation
└── scripts/            # Build and maintenance scripts
```

### Core Package: `packages/next`

The main Next.js framework lives in `packages/next/`. This is what gets published as the `next` npm package.

**Source code** is in `packages/next/src/`.

**Key entry points:**

- Dev server: `src/cli/next-dev.ts` → `src/server/dev/next-dev-server.ts`
- Production server: `src/cli/next-start.ts` → `src/server/next-server.ts`
- Build: `src/cli/next-build.ts` → `src/build/index.ts`

**Compiled output** goes to `packages/next/dist/` (mirrors src/ structure).

### Other Important Packages

- `packages/create-next-app/` - The `create-next-app` CLI tool
- `packages/next-swc/` - Native Rust bindings (SWC transforms)
- `packages/eslint-plugin-next/` - ESLint rules for Next.js
- `packages/font/` - `next/font` implementation
- `packages/third-parties/` - Third-party script integrations

### README files

Before editing or creating files in any subdirectory (e.g., `packages/*`, `crates/*`), read all `README.md` files in the directory path from the repo root up to and including the target file's directory. This helps identify any local patterns, conventions, and documentation.

**Example:** Before editing `turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/js/src/nodejs/runtime/runtime-base.ts`, read:

- `turbopack/README.md` (if exists)
- `turbopack/crates/README.md` (if exists)
- `turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/README.md` (if exists)
- `turbopack/crates/turbopack-ecmascript-runtime/js/README.md` (if exists - closest to target file)

## Build Commands

```bash
# Build the Next.js package
pnpm --filter=next build

# Build everything
pnpm build

# Run specific task
pnpm --filter=next exec taskr <task>
```

## Fast Local Development

For iterative development, default to watch mode + skip-isolate for the inner loop (not full builds), with exceptions noted below.

**Default agent rule:** If you are changing Next.js source or integration tests, start `pnpm --filter=next dev` in a separate terminal session before making edits (unless it is already running). If you skip this, explicitly state why (for example: docs-only, read-only investigation, or CI-only analysis).

**1. Start watch build in background:**

```bash
# Auto-rebuilds on file changes (~1-2s per change vs ~60s full build)
# Keep this running while you iterate on code
pnpm --filter=next dev
```

**2. Run tests fast (no isolation, no packing):**

```bash
# NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1 - skip packing Next.js for each test (~100s faster)
# testonly - runs with --runInBand (no worker isolation overhead)
NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1 NEXT_TEST_MODE=dev pnpm testonly test/path/to/test.ts
```

**3. When done, kill the background watch process (if you started it).**

**For type errors only:** Use `pnpm --filter=next types` (~10s) instead of `pnpm --filter=next build` (~60s).

After the workspace is bootstrapped, prefer `pnpm --filter=next build` when edits are limited to core Next.js files. Use full `pnpm build` for branch switches/bootstrap, before CI push, or when changes span multiple packages.

**Always run a full bootstrap build after switching branches:**

```bash
git checkout <branch>
pnpm build   # Sets up outputs for dependent packages (Turborepo dedupes if unchanged)
```

**When NOT to use NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE:** Drop it when testing module resolution changes (new require() paths, new exports from entry-base.ts, edge route imports). Without isolation, the test uses local dist/ directly, hiding resolution failures that occur when Next.js is packed as a real npm package.

## Bundler Selection

Turbopack is the default bundler for both `next dev` and `next build`. To force webpack:

```bash
next build --webpack        # Production build with webpack
next dev --webpack          # Dev server with webpack
```

There is no `--no-turbopack` flag.

## Testing

```bash
# Run specific test file (development mode with Turbopack)
pnpm test-dev-turbo test/path/to/test.test.ts

# Run tests matching pattern
pnpm test-dev-turbo -t "pattern"

# Run development tests
pnpm test-dev-turbo test/development/
```

**Test commands by mode:**

- `pnpm test-dev-turbo` - Development mode with Turbopack (default)
- `pnpm test-dev-webpack` - Development mode with Webpack
- `pnpm test-start-turbo` - Production build+start with Turbopack
- `pnpm test-start-webpack` - Production build+start with Webpack

**Other test commands:**

- `pnpm test-unit` - Run unit tests only (fast, no browser)
- `pnpm testonly <path>` - Run tests without rebuilding (faster iteration when build artifacts are already up to date)
- `pnpm new-test` - Generate a new test file from template (interactive)

**Generate tests non-interactively (for AI agents):**

Generating tests using `pnpm new-test` is mandatory.

```bash
# Use --args for non-interactive mode
# Format: pnpm new-test --args <appDir> <name> <type>
# appDir: true/false (is this for app directory?)
# name: test name (e.g. "my-feature")
# type: e2e | production | development | unit

pnpm new-test --args true my-feature e2e
```

**Analyzing test output efficiently:**

Never re-run the same test suite with different grep filters. Capture output once to a file, then read from it:

```bash
# Run once, save everything
HEADLESS=true pnpm test-dev-turbo test/path/to/test.ts > /tmp/test-output.log 2>&1

# Then analyze without re-running
grep "●" /tmp/test-output.log            # Failed test names
grep -A5 "Error:" /tmp/test-output.log   # Error details
tail -5 /tmp/test-output.log             # Summary
```

## Writing Tests

**Test writing expectations:**

- **Use `pnpm new-test` to generate new test suites** - it creates proper structure with fixture files

- **Use `retry()` from `next-test-utils` instead of `setTimeout` for waiting**

  ```typescript
  // Good - use retry() for polling/waiting
  import { retry } from 'next-test-utils'
  await retry(async () => {
    const text = await browser.elementByCss('p').text()
    expect(text).toBe('expected value')
  })

  // Bad - don't use setTimeout for waiting
  await new Promise((resolve) => setTimeout(resolve, 1000))
  ```

- **Do NOT use `check()` - it is deprecated. Use `retry()` + `expect()` instead**

  ```typescript
  // Deprecated - don't use check()
  await check(() => browser.elementByCss('p').text(), /expected/)

  // Good - use retry() with expect()
  await retry(async () => {
    const text = await browser.elementByCss('p').text()
    expect(text).toMatch(/expected/)
  })
  ```

- **Prefer real fixture directories over inline `files` objects**

  ```typescript
  // Good - use a real directory with fixture files
  const { next } = nextTestSetup({
    files: __dirname, // points to directory containing test fixtures
  })

  // Avoid - inline file definitions are harder to maintain
  const { next } = nextTestSetup({
    files: {
      'app/page.tsx': `export default function Page() { ... }`,
    },
  })
  ```

## Linting and Types

```bash
pnpm lint              # Full lint (types, prettier, eslint, ast-grep)
pnpm lint-fix          # Auto-fix lint issues
pnpm prettier-fix      # Fix formatting only
pnpm types             # TypeScript type checking
```

## PR Status (CI Failures and Reviews)

When the user asks about CI failures, PR reviews, or the status of a PR, run the pr-status script:

```bash
node scripts/pr-status.js           # Auto-detects PR from current branch
node scripts/pr-status.js <number>  # Analyze specific PR by number
```

This generates analysis files in `scripts/pr-status/`.

General triage rules (always apply; `$pr-status-triage` skill expands on these):

- Prioritize blocking failures first: build, lint, types, then tests.
- Assume failures are real until disproven; use "Known Flaky Tests" as context, not auto-dismissal.
- Reproduce with the same CI mode/env vars (especially `IS_WEBPACK_TEST=1` when present).
- For module-resolution/build-graph fixes, verify without `NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1`.

For full triage workflow (failure prioritization, mode selection, CI env reproduction, and common failure patterns), use the `$pr-status-triage` skill:

- Skill file: `.agents/skills/pr-status-triage/SKILL.md`

**Use `/pr-status` for automated analysis** - analyzes failing jobs and review comments in parallel, groups failures by test file.

**CI Analysis Tips:**

- Prioritize CI failures over review comments
- Prioritize blocking jobs first: build, lint, types, then test jobs
- Common fast checks:
  - `rust check / build` → Run `cargo fmt -- --check`, then `cargo fmt`
  - `lint / build` → Run `pnpm prettier --write <file>` for prettier errors
  - test failures → Run the specific failing test path locally

**Run tests in the right mode:**

```bash
# Dev mode (Turbopack)
pnpm test-dev-turbo test/path/to/test.ts

# Prod mode
pnpm test-start-turbo test/path/to/test.ts
```

## Key Directories (Quick Reference)

See [Codebase structure](#codebase-structure) above for detailed explanations.

- `packages/next/src/` - Main Next.js source code
- `packages/next/src/server/` - Server runtime (most changes happen here)
- `packages/next/src/client/` - Client-side runtime
- `packages/next/src/build/` - Build tooling
- `test/e2e/` - End-to-end tests
- `test/development/` - Dev server tests
- `test/production/` - Production build tests
- `test/unit/` - Unit tests (fast, no browser)

## Development Tips

- The dev server entry point is `packages/next/src/cli/next-dev.ts`
- Router server: `packages/next/src/server/lib/router-server.ts`
- Use `DEBUG=next:*` for debug logging
- Use `NEXT_TELEMETRY_DISABLED=1` when testing locally

### `NODE_ENV` vs `__NEXT_DEV_SERVER`

Both `next dev` and `next build --debug-prerender` produce bundles with `NODE_ENV=development`. Use `process.env.__NEXT_DEV_SERVER` to distinguish between them:

- `process.env.NODE_ENV !== 'production'` — code that should exist in dev bundles but be eliminated from prod bundles. This is a build-time check.
- `process.env.__NEXT_DEV_SERVER` — code that should only run with the dev server (`next dev`), not during `next build --debug-prerender` or `next start`.

## Secrets and Env Safety

Always treat environment variable values as sensitive unless they are known test-mode flags.

- Never print or paste secret values (tokens, API keys, cookies) in chat responses, commits, or shared logs.
- Mirror CI env **names and modes** exactly, but do not inline literal secret values in commands.
- If a required secret is missing locally, stop and ask the user rather than inventing placeholder credentials.
- Never commit local secret files; if documenting env setup, use placeholder-only examples.
- When sharing command output, summarize and redact sensitive-looking values.

## Specialized Skills

Use skills for conditional, deep workflows. Keep baseline iteration/build/test policy in this file.

- `$pr-status-triage` - CI failure and PR review triage with `scripts/pr-status.js`
- `$flags` - feature-flag wiring across config/schema/define-env/runtime env
- `$dce-edge` - DCE-safe `require()` patterns and edge/runtime constraints
- `$react-vendoring` - `entry-base.ts` boundaries and vendored React type/runtime rules
- `$runtime-debug` - runtime-bundle/module-resolution regression reproduction and verification
- `$authoring-skills` - how to create and maintain skills in `.agents/skills/`

## Context-Efficient Workflows

**Reading large files** (>500 lines, e.g. `app-render.tsx`):

- Grep first to find relevant line numbers, then read targeted ranges with `offset`/`limit`
- Never re-read the same section of a file without code changes in between
- For generated files (`dist/`, `node_modules/`, `.next/`): search only, don't read

**Build & test output:**

- Capture to file once, then analyze: `pnpm build 2>&1 | tee /tmp/build.log`
- Don't re-run the same test command without code changes; re-analyze saved output instead

**Batch edits before building:**

- Group related edits across files, then run one build, not build-per-edit
- Use `pnpm --filter=next types` (~10s) to check type errors without full rebuild

**External API calls (gh, curl):**

- Save response to variable or file: `JOBS=$(gh api ...) && echo "$JOBS" | jq '...'`
- Don't re-fetch the same API data to analyze from different angles

## Commit and PR Style

- Do NOT add "Generated with Claude Code" or co-author footers to commits or PRs
- Keep commit messages concise and descriptive
- PR descriptions should focus on what changed and why
- Do NOT mark PRs as "ready for review" (`gh pr ready`) - leave PRs in draft mode and let the user decide when to mark them ready

## Task Decomposition and Verification

- **Split work into smaller, individually verifiable tasks.** Before starting, break the overall goal into incremental steps where each step produces a result that can be checked independently.
- **Verify each task before moving on to the next.** After completing a step, confirm it works correctly (e.g., run relevant tests, check types, build, or manually inspect output). Do not proceed to the next task until the current one is verified.
- **Choose the right verification method for each change.** This may include running unit tests, integration tests, type checking, linting, building the project, or inspecting runtime behavior depending on what was changed.
- **When unclear how to verify a change, ask the user.** If there is no obvious test or verification method for a particular change, ask the user how they would like it verified before moving on.

**Pre-validate before committing** to avoid slow lint-staged failures (~2 min each):

```bash
# Run exactly what the pre-commit hook runs on your changed files:
pnpm prettier --with-node-modules --ignore-path .prettierignore --write <files>
npx eslint --config eslint.config.mjs --fix <files>
```

## Rebuilding Before Running Tests

When running Next.js integration tests, you must rebuild if source files have changed:

- **First run after branch switch/bootstrap (or if unsure)?** → `pnpm build`
- **Edited only core Next.js files (`packages/next/**`) after bootstrap?** → `pnpm --filter=next build`
- **Edited Turbopack (Rust)?** → `pnpm swc-build-native`
- **Edited both?** → `pnpm turbo build build-native`

## Development Anti-Patterns

For runtime internals, use focused skills:

- Feature-flag plumbing and runtime bundle wiring: `$flags` (`.agents/skills/flags/SKILL.md`)
- DCE and edge/runtime constraints: `$dce-edge` (`.agents/skills/dce-edge/SKILL.md`)
- React vendoring and `entry-base.ts` boundaries: `$react-vendoring` (`.agents/skills/react-vendoring/SKILL.md`)
- Debugging and verification workflow: `$runtime-debug` (`.agents/skills/runtime-debug/SKILL.md`)

Keep these high-frequency guardrails in mind:

- Reproduce module resolution and bundling issues without `NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1`
- Validate edge bundling regressions with `pnpm test-start-webpack test/e2e/app-dir/app/standalone.test.ts`
- Use `__NEXT_SHOW_IGNORE_LISTED=true` when you need full internal stack traces

Core runtime/bundling rules (always apply; skills above expand on these with verification steps and examples):

- New flags: add type in `config-shared.ts`, schema in `config-schema.ts`, and `define-env.ts` when used in user-bundled code.
- If a flag is consumed in pre-compiled runtime internals, also wire runtime env values (`next-server.ts`/`export/worker.ts` as needed).
- `define-env.ts` affects user bundling; it does not control pre-compiled runtime bundle internals.
- Keep `require()` behind compile-time `if/else` branches for DCE (avoid early-return/throw patterns).
- In edge builds, force feature flags that gate Node-only imports to `false` in `define-env.ts`.
- `react-server-dom-webpack/*` imports must stay in `entry-base.ts`; consume via component module exports elsewhere.

### Test Gotchas

- **Cache components enables PPR by default**: When `__NEXT_CACHE_COMPONENTS=true`, most app-dir pages use PPR implicitly. Dedicated `ppr-full/` and `ppr/` test suites are mostly `describe.skip` (migrating to cache components). To test PPR codepaths, run normal app-dir e2e tests with `__NEXT_CACHE_COMPONENTS=true` rather than looking for explicit PPR test suites.
- **Quick smoke testing with toy apps**: For fast feedback, generate a minimal test fixture with `pnpm new-test --args true <name> e2e`, then run the dev server directly with `node packages/next/dist/bin/next dev --port <port>` and `curl --max-time 10`. This avoids the overhead of the full test harness and gives immediate feedback on hangs/crashes.
- Mode-specific tests need `skipStart: true` + manual `next.start()` in `beforeAll` after mode check
- Don't rely on exact log messages - filter by content patterns, find sequences not positions
- **Snapshot tests vary by env flags**: Tests with inline snapshots can produce different output depending on env flags. When updating snapshots, always run the test with the exact env flags the CI job uses (check `.github/workflows/build_and_test.yml` `afterBuild:` sections). Turbopack resolves `react-dom/server.edge` (no Node APIs like `renderToPipeableStream`), while webpack resolves the `.node` build (has them).
- **`app-page.ts` is a build template compiled by the user's bundler**: Any `require()` in this file is traced by webpack/turbopack at `next build` time. You cannot require internal modules with relative paths because they won't be resolvable from the user's project. Instead, export new helpers from `entry-base.ts` and access them via `entryBase.*` in the template.
- **Reproducing CI failures locally**: Always match the exact CI env vars (check `pr-status` output for "Job Environment Variables"). Key differences: `IS_WEBPACK_TEST=1` forces webpack (turbopack is default), `NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE=1` skips packing next.js (hides module resolution failures). Always run without `NEXT_SKIP_ISOLATE` when verifying module resolution fixes.
- **Showing full stack traces**: Set `__NEXT_SHOW_IGNORE_LISTED=true` to disable the ignore-list filtering in dev server error output. By default, Next.js collapses internal frames to `at ignore-listed frames`, which hides useful context when debugging framework internals. Defined in `packages/next/src/server/patch-error-inspect.ts`.

### Rust/Cargo

- cargo fmt uses ASCII order (uppercase before lowercase) - just run `cargo fmt`
- **Internal compiler error (ICE)?** Delete incremental compilation artifacts and retry. Remove `*/incremental` directories from your cargo target directory (default `target/`, or check `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` env var)

### Node.js Source Maps

- `findSourceMap()` needs `--enable-source-maps` flag or returns undefined
- Source map paths vary (webpack: `./src/`, tsc: `src/`) - try multiple formats
- `process.cwd()` in stack trace formatting produces different paths in tests vs production

### Stale Native Binary

If Turbopack produces unexpected errors after switching branches or pulling, check if `packages/next-swc/native/*.node` is stale. Delete it and run `pnpm install` to get the npm-published binary instead of a locally-built one.

### Documentation Code Blocks

- When adding `highlight={...}` attributes to code blocks, carefully count the actual line numbers within the code block
- Account for empty lines, import statements, and type imports that shift line numbers
- Highlights should point to the actual relevant code, not unrelated lines like `return (` or framework boilerplate
- Double-check highlights by counting lines from 1 within each code block

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to AI assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, etc.)
when working with code in this repository.

## Project Overview

Better Auth is a comprehensive, framework-agnostic authentication
framework for TypeScript.

## Development Commands

```bash
# Install dependencies
pnpm install

# Build all packages
pnpm build

# Run all tests
pnpm test

# Lint code
pnpm lint

# Fix linting issues
pnpm lint:fix

# Type check
pnpm typecheck
```

Do not run `pnpm test` directly because it runs tests in all packages,
which takes a long time, use `vitest /path/to/<test-file> -t <pattern>` to
run specific tests.

## Architecture

### Package Structure

* `packages/better-auth` - Main authentication library
* `packages/core` - Core utilities and types
* `packages/cli` - Command-line interface
* `packages/*` - Various plugins and integrations

## Code Style

* Formatter: Biome (tabs for code, 2-space for JSON)
* Avoid unsafe typecasts or types like `any`
* Avoid classes, use functions and objects
* Do not use runtime-specific feature like `Buffer` in codebase except
  test, use `Uint8Array` instead

## Testing

* Most of the tests use Vitest
* Some tests under `e2e` directory use playwright
* Adapter tests require Docker containers running (`docker compose up -d`)
* Consider using test helpers like `getTestInstance()` from
  `better-auth/test` first
* If a test is to prevent regression of a specific numbered GitHub issue,
  add a JSDoc `@see` comment with the issue URL above the `it()` or `describe()`:
  ```typescript
  /**
   * @see https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth/issues/{issue_number}
   */
  it("should handle the previously broken behavior", async () => {
    // ...
  });
  ```

## Documentation

* Please update the documentation when you make changes to the public API
* Documentation is located in the `docs/` directory, built with
  [Next.js](https://nextjs.org/docs/llms.txt) + [Fumadocs](https://www.fumadocs.dev/llms.txt)

## Git Workflow

* PRs should target the `canary` branch
* Commit format: `feat(scope): description` or `fix(scope): description`,
  following [Conventional Commits](https://www.conventionalcommits.org/en/v1.0.0/)
* Use `docs:` for documentation, `chore:` for non-functional changes

## Postmortems

Check `postmortem/` directory for lessons learned from past issues.

## After Everything is done

**Unless the user asked for it or you are working on CI, DO NOT COMMIT**

* Make sure `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` pass

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

---

> **⚠️ IMPORTANT: Context Discovery**
>
> Before modifying files in any directory, **always check for a `CLAUDE.md` file in that directory** and read it first.
> When asked to work on a specific directory, look for and read `CLAUDE.md` in that directory before starting.
> These nested context files contain directory-specific conventions and patterns that override or extend this file.

---

## Commands

```bash
# Development
pnpm dev              # Start all apps in dev mode
pnpm dev:web          # Start Next.js web app (localhost:3001)
pnpm dev:native       # Start Expo mobile app

# Build & Type Check
pnpm build            # Build all apps
pnpm check-types      # TypeScript type check across all packages

# Linting & Formatting
pnpm check            # Run Biome lint and format with auto-fix

# Database (Drizzle)
pnpm db:push          # Push schema changes to database
pnpm db:generate      # Generate migrations
pnpm db:migrate       # Run migrations
pnpm db:studio        # Open Drizzle Studio UI
pnpm db:start         # Start local database (if using Docker)
pnpm db:stop          # Stop local database
```

## Architecture

Turborepo monorepo with pnpm workspaces containing:

### Apps
- **`apps/web`** - Next.js 16 fullstack app with App Router, React 19, TailwindCSS, shadcn/ui
- **`apps/native`** - Expo/React Native mobile app with Expo Router, NativeWind/TailwindCSS

### Packages
- **`packages/api`** - oRPC router definitions and procedures (type-safe API layer)
- **`packages/auth`** - Better Auth configuration with Polar payments integration
- **`packages/db`** - Drizzle ORM schema and database client (PostgreSQL)
- **`packages/env`** - Environment variable validation using @t3-oss/env-core
- **`packages/config`** - Shared TypeScript configurations

### Data Flow
```
[Web/Native Client]
       ↓
   oRPC Client (TanStack Query)
       ↓
  /api/rpc/[[...rest]] (Next.js route)
       ↓
   createContext() → auth.api.getSession()
       ↓
   AppRouter procedures
       ↓
   Drizzle ORM → PostgreSQL
```

## Key Patterns

### oRPC Procedures
- Base procedures defined in `packages/api/src/index.ts`
- `publicProcedure` - no auth required
- `protectedProcedure` - requires authenticated session
- Routers in `packages/api/src/routers/` are merged into `appRouter`

### Adding a New API Procedure
1. Create or extend router in `packages/api/src/routers/`
2. Export from `packages/api/src/routers/index.ts`
3. Type is automatically inferred by clients via `AppRouterClient`

### Database Schema
- Schema files in `packages/db/src/schema/`
- Drizzle config reads `.env` from `apps/web/.env`
- Use `pnpm db:push` for prototyping, `pnpm db:generate && db:migrate` for production

### Environment Variables
- Server env (DATABASE_URL, BETTER_AUTH_SECRET, etc.): `packages/env/src/server.ts`
- Web client env: `packages/env/src/web.ts`
- Native client env (EXPO_PUBLIC_*): `packages/env/src/native.ts`

### Authentication
- Better Auth with email/password, Polar payments, Expo support
- Auth client: `apps/web/src/lib/auth-client.ts` or `apps/native/lib/auth-client.ts`
- Session available in oRPC context via `createContext()`

## Required Environment Variables

Create `apps/web/.env`:
```
DATABASE_URL=postgresql://...
BETTER_AUTH_SECRET=<32+ chars>
BETTER_AUTH_URL=http://localhost:3001
POLAR_ACCESS_TOKEN=...
POLAR_SUCCESS_URL=http://localhost:3001/success
CORS_ORIGIN=http://localhost:3001
```

For native app, create `apps/native/.env`:
```
EXPO_PUBLIC_SERVER_URL=http://localhost:3001
```

## Code Style

- Biome for linting and formatting (tab indents, double quotes)
- `pnpm check` auto-fixes lint issues and sorts imports
- Tailwind class sorting enabled via Biome nursery rule

# Documentation Worktrees Setup

## Context

Set up 4 documentation/reference repositories for learning latest patterns from key dependencies:
- **shadcn/ui** - UI component patterns
- **Next.js** - App Router, RSC, data patterns
- **oRPC** - Type-safe API patterns (current project dependency)
- **Better Auth** - Authentication patterns (current project dependency)

These repos serve as read-only reference material for understanding best practices and latest features.

---

## Repository URLs

| Library | GitHub URL |
|---------|------------|
| shadcn/ui | https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui |
| Next.js | https://github.com/vercel/next.js |
| oRPC | https://github.com/middleapi/orpc |
| Better Auth | https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth |

---

## Directory Structure

```
/Users/orksys/Projects/
├── docs-worktrees/
│   ├── shadcn-ui/
│   │   └── CLAUDE.md
│   ├── nextjs/
│   │   └── CLAUDE.md
│   ├── orpc/
│   │   └── CLAUDE.md
│   └── better-auth/
│       └── CLAUDE.md
├── orksys-survey/          (main project)
└── ... (other projects)
```

---

## Implementation Steps

### Step 1: Create parent directory
```bash
mkdir -p /Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees
```

### Step 2: Clone repositories (shallow clones)
```bash
cd /Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees

# shadcn/ui - UI components
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/shadcn-ui/ui.git shadcn-ui

# Next.js - Framework
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/vercel/next.js.git nextjs

# oRPC - Type-safe RPC
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/middleapi/orpc.git orpc

# Better Auth - Authentication
git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/better-auth/better-auth.git better-auth
```

### Step 3: Create CLAUDE.md for each repo

**shadcn-ui/CLAUDE.md:**
```markdown
# shadcn/ui Documentation Worktree

This is a **documentation and research worktree** for shadcn/ui.

## Purpose
- Learn latest component patterns and APIs
- Reference for base-ui primitives usage
- Study styling conventions (base-nova theme)

## Key Directories
- `apps/www/` - Documentation site
- `packages/shadcn/` - Core component source
- `packages/ui/` - UI components

## Usage
Read-only reference. Do not make changes.
Update with: `git pull origin main`
```

**nextjs/CLAUDE.md:**
```markdown
# Next.js Documentation Worktree

This is a **documentation and research worktree** for Next.js.

## Purpose
- Learn App Router patterns
- Study React Server Components
- Reference for data fetching and caching

## Key Directories
- `docs/` - Documentation source
- `packages/next/` - Framework source
- `examples/` - Example applications

## Usage
Read-only reference. Do not make changes.
Update with: `git pull origin main`
```

**orpc/CLAUDE.md:**
```markdown
# oRPC Documentation Worktree

This is a **documentation and research worktree** for oRPC.

## Purpose
- Study type-safe API patterns
- Reference for oRPC client/server setup
- Learn best practices for procedure definitions

## Key Directories
- `packages/` - Core packages
- `examples/` - Example implementations
- `docs/` - Documentation

## Usage
Read-only reference. Do not make changes.
Update with: `git pull origin main`
```

**better-auth/CLAUDE.md:**
```markdown
# Better Auth Documentation Worktree

This is a **documentation and research worktree** for Better Auth.

## Purpose
- Study authentication patterns
- Reference for plugin configurations
- Learn session management best practices

## Key Directories
- `packages/better-auth/` - Core package
- `packages/*` - Plugins
- `docs/` - Documentation
- `examples/` - Example implementations

## Usage
Read-only reference. Do not make changes.
Update with: `git pull origin main`
```

---

## Files to Create

| Path | Action |
|------|--------|
| `/Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees/` | Create directory |
| `/Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees/shadcn-ui/` | Clone repo |
| `/Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees/shadcn-ui/CLAUDE.md` | Create |
| `/Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees/nextjs/` | Clone repo |
| `/Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees/nextjs/CLAUDE.md` | Create |
| `/Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees/orpc/` | Clone repo |
| `/Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees/orpc/CLAUDE.md` | Create |
| `/Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees/better-auth/` | Clone repo |
| `/Users/orksys/Projects/docs-worktrees/better-auth/CLAUDE.md` | Create |

---

## Verification

1. Verify all 4 directories exist with repos cloned
2. Verify each has a CLAUDE.md file
3. Test reading a file from each repo
4. Verify shallow clone worked: `cd nextjs && git log --oneline | wc -l` should show 1

---

## Notes

- Using **shallow clones** (`--depth 1`) because:
  - Only need latest code for reference
  - Significantly smaller disk usage (Next.js repo is huge)
  - Faster clone times
  - Can still update with `git pull`

- These are **not** true git worktrees linked to a main repo. For documentation purposes, simple clones are more practical and easier to maintain.

1→import { relations } from "drizzle-orm";
     2→import {
     3→	index,
     4→	json,
     5→	pgEnum,
     6→	pgTable,
     7→	text,
     8→	timestamp,
     9→	uniqueIndex,
    10→} from "drizzle-orm/pg-core";
    11→
    12→import { user } from "./auth";
    13→
    14→// Member role enum
    15→export const memberRoleEnum = pgEnum("member_role", [
    16→	"owner",
    17→	"admin",
    18→	"member",
    19→]);
    20→
    21→// Invitation status enum
    22→export const invitationStatusEnum = pgEnum("invitation_status", [
    23→	"pending",
    24→	"accepted",
    25→	"rejected",
    26→	"expired",
    27→]);
    28→
    29→// Organization table
    30→export const organization = pgTable(
    31→	"organization",
    32→	{
    33→		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
    34→		name: text("name").notNull(),
    35→		slug: text("slug").notNull(),
    36→		logo: text("logo"),
    37→		metadata: json("metadata").$type<OrganizationMetadata>(),
    38→		createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
    39→		updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at")
    40→			.defaultNow()
    41→			.$onUpdate(() => new Date())
    42→			.notNull(),
    43→	},
    44→	(table) => [uniqueIndex("organization_slug_idx").on(table.slug)],
    45→);
    46→
    47→// Member table
    48→export const member = pgTable(
    49→	"member",
    50→	{
    51→		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
    52→		userId: text("user_id")
    53→			.notNull()
    54→			.references(() => user.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    55→		organizationId: text("organization_id")
    56→			.notNull()
    57→			.references(() => organization.id, { onDelete: "cascade" }),
    58→		role: memberRoleEnum("role").default("member").notNull(),
    59→		createdAt: timestamp("created_at").defaultNow().notNull(),
    60→		updatedAt: timestamp("updated_at")
    61→			.defaultNow()
    62→			.$onUpdate(() => new Date())
    63→			.notNull(),
    64→	},
    65→	(table) => [
    66→		index("member_userId_idx").on(table.userId),
    67→		index("member_organizationId_idx").on(table.organizationId),
    68→		uniqueIndex("member_user_organization_idx").on(
    69→			table.userId,
    70→			table.organizationId,
    71→		),
    72→	],
    73→);
    74→
    75→// Invitation table
    76→export const invitation = pgTable(
    77→	"invitation",
    78→	{
    79→		id: text("id").primaryKey(),
    80→		email: text("email").notNull(),

1→--- 2→title: Organization 3→description: The organization plugin allows you to manage your organization's members and teams. 4→--- 5→ 6→Organizations simplifies user access and permissions management. Assign roles and permissions to streamline project management, team coordination, and partnerships. 7→ 8→## Installation 9→ 10→ 11→ 12→### Add the plugin to your **auth** config 13→```ts title="auth.ts" 14→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth" 15→import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins" // [!code highlight] 16→ 17→export const auth = betterAuth({ 18→ plugins: [ 19→ organization() // [!code highlight] 20→ ] 21→}) 22→``` 23→ 24→ 25→ 26→ ### Migrate the database 27→ 28→ Run the migration or generate the schema to add the necessary fields and tables to the database. 29→ 30→ 31→ 32→ ```package-install 33→ npx auth migrate 34→ ``` 35→ 36→ 37→ ```package-install 38→ npx auth generate 39→ ``` 40→ 41→ 42→ See the [Schema](#schema) section to add the fields manually. 43→ 44→ 45→ 46→ 47→ ### Add the client plugin 48→ 49→ ```ts title="auth-client.ts" 50→ import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client" 51→ import { organizationClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins" // [!code highlight] 52→ 53→ export const authClient = createAuthClient({ 54→ plugins: [ 55→ organizationClient() // [!code highlight] 56→ ] 57→ }) 58→ ``` 59→ 60→ 61→ 62→ 63→## Usage 64→ 65→Once you've installed the plugin, you can start using the organization plugin to manage your organization's members and teams. The client plugin will provide you with methods under the `organization` namespace, and the server `api` will provide you with the necessary endpoints to manage your organization and give you an easier way to call the functions on your own backend. 66→ 67→## Organization 68→ 69→### Create an organization 70→ 71→ 72→ 73→```ts 74→const metadata = { someKey: "someValue" }; 75→ 76→type createOrganization = { 77→ /** 78→ * The organization name. 79→ */ 80→ name: string = "My Organization" 81→ /** 82→ * The organization slug. 83→ */ 84→ slug: string = "my-org" 85→ /** 86→ * The organization logo. 87→ */ 88→ logo?: string = "https://example.com/logo.png" 89→ /** 90→ * The metadata of the organization. 91→ */ 92→ metadata?: Record 93→ /** 94→ * The user ID of the organization creator. 95→ * @serverOnly - This is ignored if session headers are provided. 96→ */ 97→ userId?: string = "some_user_id" 98→ /** 99→ * Whether to keep the current active organization active after creating a new one. 100→ */ 101→ keepCurrentActiveOrganization?: boolean = false 102→} 103→``` 104→ 105→ 106→ 107→ 108→**Mutually Exclusive Parameters** 109→ 110→The `userId` and session headers cannot be used together: 111→- **With session headers:** The organization is created for the authenticated session user. The `userId` field is **silently ignored**. 112→- **Without session headers (Server-side only):** The organization is created for the user specified by `userId`. 113→ 114→**For Admins:** To create an organization on behalf of another user, you must make the API call server-side **without** passing session headers. 115→ 116→ 117→#### Restrict who can create an organization 118→ 119→By default, any user can create an organization. To restrict this, set the `allowUserToCreateOrganization` option to a function that returns a boolean, or directly to `true` or `false`. 120→ 121→```ts title="auth.ts" 122→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"; 123→import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins"; 124→ 125→const auth = betterAuth({ 126→ //... 127→ plugins: [ 128→ organization({ 129→ allowUserToCreateOrganization: async (user) => { // [!code highlight] 130→ const subscription = await getSubscription(user.id); // [!code highlight] 131→ return subscription.plan === "pro"; // [!code highlight] 132→ }, // [!code highlight] 133→ }), 134→ ], 135→}); 136→``` 137→ 138→#### Check if organization slug is taken 139→ 140→To check if an organization slug is taken or not you can use the `checkSlug` function provided by the client. The function takes an object with the following properties: 141→ 142→ 143→```ts 144→type checkOrganizationSlug = { 145→ /** 146→ * The organization slug to check. 147→ */ 148→ slug: string = "my-org" 149→} 150→``` 151→ 152→ 153→### Organization Hooks 154→ 155→You can customize organization operations using hooks that run before and after various organization-related activities. Better Auth provides two ways to configure hooks: 156→ 157→1. **Legacy organizationCreation hooks** (deprecated, use `organizationHooks` instead) 158→2. **Modern organizationHooks** (recommended) - provides comprehensive control over all organization-related activities 159→ 160→#### Organization Creation and Management Hooks 161→ 162→Control organization lifecycle operations: 163→ 164→```ts title="auth.ts" 165→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"; 166→import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins"; 167→ 168→export const auth = betterAuth({ 169→ plugins: [ 170→ organization({ 171→ organizationHooks: { 172→ // Organization creation hooks 173→ beforeCreateOrganization: async ({ organization, user }) => { 174→ // Run custom logic before organization is created 175→ // Optionally modify the organization data 176→ return { 177→ data: { 178→ ...organization, 179→ metadata: { 180→ customField: "value", 181→ }, 182→ }, 183→ }; 184→ }, 185→ 186→ afterCreateOrganization: async ({ organization, member, user }) => { 187→ // Run custom logic after organization is created 188→ // e.g., create default resources, send notifications 189→ await setupDefaultResources(organization.id); 190→ }, 191→ 192→ // Organization update hooks 193→ beforeUpdateOrganization: async ({ organization, user, member }) => { 194→ // Validate updates, apply business rules 195→ return { 196→ data: { 197→ ...organization, 198→ name: organization.name?.toLowerCase(), 199→ }, 200→ }; 201→ }, 202→ 203→ afterUpdateOrganization: async ({ organization, user, member }) => { 204→ // Sync changes to external systems 205→ await syncOrganizationToExternalSystems(organization); 206→ }, 207→ }, 208→ }), 209→ ], 210→}); 211→``` 212→ 213→ 214→ The legacy `organizationCreation` hooks are still supported but deprecated. 215→ Use `organizationHooks.beforeCreateOrganization` and 216→ `organizationHooks.afterCreateOrganization` instead for new projects. 217→ 218→ 219→#### Member Hooks 220→ 221→Control member operations within organizations: 222→ 223→```ts title="auth.ts" 224→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"; 225→import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins"; 226→ 227→export const auth = betterAuth({ 228→ plugins: [ 229→ organization({ 230→ organizationHooks: { 231→ // Before a member is added to an organization 232→ beforeAddMember: async ({ member, user, organization }) => { 233→ // Custom validation or modification 234→ console.log(`Adding ${user.email} to ${organization.name}`); 235→ 236→ // Optionally modify member data 237→ return { 238→ data: { 239→ ...member, 240→ role: "custom-role", // Override the role 241→ }, 242→ }; 243→ }, 244→ 245→ // After a member is added 246→ afterAddMember: async ({ member, user, organization }) => { 247→ // Send welcome email, create default resources, etc. 248→ await sendWelcomeEmail(user.email, organization.name); 249→ }, 250→ 251→ // Before a member is removed 252→ beforeRemoveMember: async ({ member, user, organization }) => { 253→ // Cleanup user's resources, send notification, etc. 254→ await cleanupUserResources(user.id, organization.id); 255→ }, 256→ 257→ // After a member is removed 258→ afterRemoveMember: async ({ member, user, organization }) => { 259→ await logMemberRemoval(user.id, organization.id); 260→ }, 261→ 262→ // Before updating a member's role 263→ beforeUpdateMemberRole: async ({ 264→ member, 265→ newRole, 266→ user, 267→ organization, 268→ }) => { 269→ // Validate role change permissions 270→ if (newRole === "owner" && !hasOwnerUpgradePermission(user)) { 271→ throw new Error("Cannot upgrade to owner role"); 272→ } 273→ 274→ // Optionally modify the role 275→ return { 276→ data: { 277→ role: newRole, 278→ }, 279→ }; 280→ }, 281→ 282→ // After updating a member's role 283→ afterUpdateMemberRole: async ({ 284→ member, 285→ previousRole, 286→ user, 287→ organization, 288→ }) => { 289→ await logRoleChange(user.id, previousRole, member.role); 290→ }, 291→ }, 292→ }), 293→ ], 294→}); 295→``` 296→ 297→#### Invitation Hooks 298→ 299→Control invitation lifecycle: 300→ 301→```ts title="auth.ts" 302→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"; 303→import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins"; 304→ 305→export const auth = betterAuth({ 306→ plugins: [ 307→ organization({ 308→ organizationHooks: { 309→ // Before creating an invitation 310→ beforeCreateInvitation: async ({ 311→ invitation, 312→ inviter, 313→ organization, 314→ }) => { 315→ // Custom validation or expiration logic 316→ const customExpiration = new Date( 317→ Date.now() + 1000 * 60 * 60 * 24 * 7 318→ ); // 7 days 319→ 320→ return { 321→ data: { 322→ ...invitation, 323→ expiresAt: customExpiration, 324→ }, 325→ }; 326→ }, 327→ 328→ // After creating an invitation 329→ afterCreateInvitation: async ({ 330→ invitation, 331→ inviter, 332→ organization, 333→ }) => { 334→ // Send custom invitation email, track metrics, etc. 335→ await sendCustomInvitationEmail(invitation, organization); 336→ }, 337→ 338→ // Before accepting an invitation 339→ beforeAcceptInvitation: async ({ invitation, user, organization }) => { 340→ // Additional validation before acceptance 341→ await validateUserEligibility(user, organization); 342→ }, 343→ 344→ // After accepting an invitation 345→ afterAcceptInvitation: async ({ 346→ invitation, 347→ member, 348→ user, 349→ organization, 350→ }) => { 351→ // Setup user account, assign default resources 352→ await setupNewMemberResources(user, organization); 353→ }, 354→ 355→ // Before/after rejecting invitations 356→ beforeRejectInvitation: async ({ invitation, user, organization }) => { 357→ // Log rejection reason, send notification to inviter 358→ }, 359→ 360→ afterRejectInvitation: async ({ invitation, user, organization }) => { 361→ await notifyInviterOfRejection(invitation.inviterId, user.email); 362→ }, 363→ 364→ // Before/after cancelling invitations 365→ beforeCancelInvitation: async ({ 366→ invitation, 367→ cancelledBy, 368→ organization, 369→ }) => { 370→ // Verify cancellation permissions 371→ }, 372→ 373→ afterCancelInvitation: async ({ 374→ invitation, 375→ cancelledBy, 376→ organization, 377→ }) => { 378→ await logInvitationCancellation(invitation.id, cancelledBy.id); 379→ }, 380→ }, 381→ }), 382→ ], 383→}); 384→``` 385→ 386→#### Team Hooks 387→ 388→Control team operations (when teams are enabled): 389→ 390→```ts title="auth.ts" 391→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"; 392→import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins"; 393→ 394→export const auth = betterAuth({ 395→ plugins: [ 396→ organization({ 397→ teams: { enabled: true }, 398→ organizationHooks: { 399→ // Before creating a team 400→ beforeCreateTeam: async ({ team, user, organization }) => { 401→ // Validate team name, apply naming conventions 402→ return { 403→ data: { 404→ ...team, 405→ name: team.name.toLowerCase().replace(/\s+/g, "-"), 406→ }, 407→ }; 408→ }, 409→ 410→ // After creating a team 411→ afterCreateTeam: async ({ team, user, organization }) => { 412→ // Create default team resources, channels, etc. 413→ await createDefaultTeamResources(team.id); 414→ }, 415→ 416→ // Before updating a team 417→ beforeUpdateTeam: async ({ team, updates, user, organization }) => { 418→ // Validate updates, apply business rules 419→ return { 420→ data: { 421→ ...updates, 422→ name: updates.name?.toLowerCase(), 423→ }, 424→ }; 425→ }, 426→ 427→ // After updating a team 428→ afterUpdateTeam: async ({ team, user, organization }) => { 429→ await syncTeamChangesToExternalSystems(team); 430→ }, 431→ 432→ // Before deleting a team 433→ beforeDeleteTeam: async ({ team, user, organization }) => { 434→ // Backup team data, notify members 435→ await backupTeamData(team.id); 436→ }, 437→ 438→ // After deleting a team 439→ afterDeleteTeam: async ({ team, user, organization }) => { 440→ await cleanupTeamResources(team.id); 441→ }, 442→ 443→ // Team member operations 444→ beforeAddTeamMember: async ({ 445→ teamMember, 446→ team, 447→ user, 448→ organization, 449→ }) => { 450→ // Validate team membership limits, permissions 451→ const memberCount = await getTeamMemberCount(team.id); 452→ if (memberCount >= 10) { 453→ throw new Error("Team is full"); 454→ } 455→ }, 456→ 457→ afterAddTeamMember: async ({ 458→ teamMember, 459→ team, 460→ user, 461→ organization, 462→ }) => { 463→ await grantTeamAccess(user.id, team.id); 464→ }, 465→ 466→ beforeRemoveTeamMember: async ({ 467→ teamMember, 468→ team, 469→ user, 470→ organization, 471→ }) => { 472→ // Backup user's team-specific data 473→ await backupTeamMemberData(user.id, team.id); 474→ }, 475→ 476→ afterRemoveTeamMember: async ({ 477→ teamMember, 478→ team, 479→ user, 480→ organization, 481→ }) => { 482→ await revokeTeamAccess(user.id, team.id); 483→ }, 484→ }, 485→ }), 486→ ], 487→}); 488→``` 489→ 490→#### Hook Error Handling 491→ 492→All hooks support error handling. Throwing an error in a `before` hook will prevent the operation from proceeding: 493→ 494→```ts title="auth.ts" 495→import { betterAuth } from "better-auth"; 496→import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins"; 497→import { APIError } from "better-auth/api"; 498→ 499→export const auth = betterAuth({ 500→ plugins: [ 501→ organization({ 502→ organizationHooks: { 503→ beforeAddMember: async ({ member, user, organization }) => { 504→ // Check if user has pending violations 505→ const violations = await checkUserViolations(user.id); 506→ if (violations.length > 0) { 507→ throw new APIError("BAD_REQUEST", { 508→ message: 509→ "User has pending violations and cannot join organizations", 510→ }); 511→ } 512→ }, 513→ 514→ beforeCreateTeam: async ({ team, user, organization }) => { 515→ // Validate team name uniqueness 516→ const existingTeam = await findTeamByName(team.name, organization.id); 517→ if (existingTeam) { 518→ throw new APIError("BAD_REQUEST", { 519→ message: "Team name already exists in this organization", 520→ }); 521→ } 522→ }, 523→ }, 524→ }), 525→ ], 526→}); 527→``` 528→ 529→### List User's Organizations 530→ 531→To list the organizations that a user is a member of, you can use `useListOrganizations` hook. You can control the access of the user based on the role they have in the organization. You can define your own set of permissions based on the role of the user. 1229→ 1230→### Roles 1231→ 1232→By default, there are three roles in the organization: 1233→ 1234→`owner`: The user who created the organization by default. The owner has full control over the organization and can perform any action. 1235→ 1236→`admin`: Users with the admin role have full control over the organization except for deleting the organization or changing the owner. 1237→ 1238→`member`: Users with the member role have limited control over the organization. They can only read organization data and have no permissions to create, update, or delete resources. 1239→ 1240→ 1241→ A user can have multiple roles. Multiple roles are stored as string separated 1242→ by comma (","). 1243→ 1244→ 1245→### Permissions 1246→ 1247→By default, there are three resources, and these have two to three actions. 1248→ 1249→**organization**: 1250→ 1251→ `update` `delete` 1252→ 1253→**member**: 1254→ 1255→ `create` `update` `delete` 1256→ 1257→**invitation**: 1258→ 1259→ `create` `cancel` 1260→ 1261→The owner has full control over all the resources and actions. The admin has full control over all the resources except for deleting the organization or changing the owner. The member has no control over any of those actions other than reading the data. 1262→ 1263→### Custom Permissions 1264→ 1265→The plugin provides an easy way to define your own set of permissions for each role. 1266→ 1267→ 1268→ 1269→ #### Create Access Control 1270→ 1271→ You first need to create access controller by calling `createAccessControl` function and passing the statement object. The statement object should have the resource name as the key and the array of actions as the value. 1272→ ```ts title="permissions.ts" 1273→ import { createAccessControl } from "better-auth/plugins/access"; 1274→ 1275→ /** 1276→ * make sure to use `as const` so typescript can infer the type correctly 1277→ */ 1278→ const statement = { // [!code highlight] 1279→ project: ["create", "share", "update", "delete"], // [!code highlight] 1280→ } as const; // [!code highlight] 1281→ 1282→ const ac = createAccessControl(statement); // [!code highlight] 1283→ ``` 1284→ 1285→ 1286→ To keep bundle sizes small, make sure to import from `better-auth/plugins/access` instead of `better-auth/plugins`. 1287→ 1288→ 1289→ 1290→ 1291→ #### Create Roles 1292→ 1293→ Once you have created the access controller you can create roles with the permissions you have defined. 1294→ 1295→ ```ts title="permissions.ts" 1296→ import { createAccessControl } from "better-auth/plugins/access"; 1297→ 1298→ const statement = { 1299→ project: ["create", "share", "update", "delete"], 1300→ } as const; 1301→ 1302→ const ac = createAccessControl(statement); 1303→ 1304→ const member = ac.newRole({ // [!code highlight] 1305→ project: ["create"], // [!code highlight] 1306→ }); // [!code highlight] 1307→ 1308→ const admin = ac.newRole({ // [!code highlight] 1309→ project: ["create", "update"], // [!code highlight] 1310→ }); // [!code highlight] 1311→ 1312→ const owner = ac.newRole({ // [!code highlight] 1313→ project: ["create", "update", "delete"], // [!code highlight] 1314→ }); // [!code highlight] 1315→ 1316→ const myCustomRole = ac.newRole({ // [!code highlight] 1317→ project: ["create", "update", "delete"], // [!code highlight] 1318→ organization: ["update"], // [!code highlight] 1319→ }); // [!code highlight] 1320→ ``` 1321→ 1322→ When you create custom roles for existing roles, the predefined permissions for those roles will be overridden. To add the existing permissions to the custom role, you need to import `defaultStatements` and merge it with your new statement, plus merge the roles' permissions set with the default roles. 1323→ 1324→ ```ts title="permissions.ts" 1325→ import { createAccessControl } from "better-auth/plugins/access"; 1326→ import { defaultStatements, adminAc } from 'better-auth/plugins/organization/access' 1327→ 1328→ const statement = { 1329→ ...defaultStatements, // [!code highlight] 1330→ project: ["create", "share", "update", "delete"], 1331→ } as const; 1332→ 1333→ const ac = createAccessControl(statement); 1334→ 1335→ const admin = ac.newRole({ 1336→ project: ["create", "update"], 1337→ ...adminAc.statements, // [!code highlight] 1338→ }); 1339→ ``` 1340→ 1341→ 1342→ 1343→ 1344→ #### Pass Roles to the Plugin 1345→ 1346→ Once you have created the roles you can pass them to the organization plugin both on the client and the server. 1347→ 1348→ ```ts title="auth.ts" 1349→ import { betterAuth } from "better-auth" 1350→ import { organization } from "better-auth/plugins" 1351→ import { ac, owner, admin, member } from "@/auth/permissions" 1352→ 1353→ export const auth = betterAuth({ 1354→ plugins: [ 1355→ organization({ 1356→ ac, 1357→ roles: { 1358→ owner, 1359→ admin, 1360→ member, 1361→ myCustomRole 1362→ } 1363→ }), 1364→ ], 1365→ }); 1366→ ``` 1367→ 1368→ You also need to pass the access controller and the roles to the client plugin. 1369→ 1370→ ```ts title="auth-client" 1371→ import { createAuthClient } from "better-auth/client" 1372→ import { organizationClient } from "better-auth/client/plugins" 1373→ import { ac, owner, admin, member, myCustomRole } from "@/auth/permissions" 1374→ 1375→ export const authClient = createAuthClient({ 1376→ plugins: [ 1377→ organizationClient({ 1378→ ac, 1379→ roles: { 1380→ owner, 1381→ admin, 1382→ member, 1383→ myCustomRole 1384→ } 1385→ }) 1386→ ] 1387→ }) 1388→ ``` 1389→ 1390→ 1391→ 1392→ 1393→### Access Control Usage 1394→ 1395→**Has Permission**: 1396→ 1397→You can use the `hasPermission` action provided by the `api` to check the permission of the user. 1398→ 1399→```ts title="has-permission.ts" 1400→import { auth } from "@/lib/auth" 1401→ 1402→await auth.api.hasPermission({ 1403→ headers: await headers(), 1404→ body: { 1405→ permissions: { 1406→ project: ["create"], // This must match the structure in your access control 1407→ }, 1408→ }, 1409→}); 1410→ 1411→// You can also check multiple resource permissions at the same time 1412→await auth.api.hasPermission({ 1413→ headers: await headers(), 1414→ body: { 1415→ permissions: { 1416→ project: ["create"], // This must match the structure in your access control 1417→ sale: ["create"], 1418→ }, 1419→ }, 1420→}); 1421→``` 1422→ 1423→If you want to check the permission of the user on the client from the server you can use the `hasPermission` function provided by the client. 1424→ 1425→```ts title="auth-client.ts" 1426→const canCreateProject = await authClient.organization.hasPermission({ 1427→ permissions: { 1428→ project: ["create"], 1429→ }, 1430→}); 1431→ 1432→// You can also check multiple resource permissions at the same time 1433→const canCreateProjectAndCreateSale = 1434→ await authClient.organization.hasPermission({ 1435→ permissions: { 1436→ project: ["create"], 1437→ sale: ["create"], 1438→ }, 1439→ });
